notice: Generated by `go test ./internal/cdreason/ -run TestCDReadyReasonTableIsCurrent` in go/core-provider, with UPDATE_READY_REASONS=1 to rewrite it, from the same registry as docs/cd-ready-reasons.md. Do not edit by hand. There is one entry per condition, status and reason: look a CompositionDefinition's condition up by those three. Where two writers write the same condition, status and reason (the markdown has a row for each), the entry lists both under writers and gives each one's meaning, clearance, sinceVersion, action and detail fields under cases. The writer cannot be determined from the object, so present the entry's own clearance and action, which are those of its longest-lasting case (indefinite, then timer, then next pass, then steady), and show the condition's message only as detail. Renaming or removing a reason, or changing its status, is a breaking change for consumers: it is done only by listing the old reason under deprecated, with the release it was removed in, and a test refuses any other removal. The set is CLOSED. verdict is how a parent composition's rollup reads a CompositionDefinition child carrying the reason: healthy, converging, failed or unevaluated, and null on a condition the rollup does not read (only Ready is read); an unevaluated entry also carries rollsUpAs, the verdict it counts as. clearance.kind is one of four: steady (an end state, not expected to clear), timer (clears when an operation returns, bounded by a named timer; core-provider names none today, so no entry here has it), next pass (clears on the next reconcile once its cause is gone) or indefinite (lasts until something outside the controller changes); clearance.detail says what clears it, with any bound in words. The markdown has no column for it. sinceVersion is the first core-provider release whose source (with its pinned runtime) contains the reason, a lower bound for a reason string another condition used first; "unreleased" until a release ships it. action is what a person does, in plain words; it is shown on screen, so changing it is a UI change. actors says who must act, a non-empty list of you (the person reading the portal), admin (an admin of the cluster) and maintainers (the blueprint's): present on every action that is not a wait and on a wait whose step is a portal control, absent otherwise; a control is pressed by you or admin. control, when present, is the on-screen label of the portal control that does the step (Resume, or Clear create-pending annotation). annotation, when present, is the annotation the step changes, {name, op, value}: op is remove (no value), set (value required: the value to set) or edit (no value: the person chooses it, and the action's words say what to allow); show it under Details, never in the action. The entry's top-level clearance, action, control and annotation are authoritative for on-screen text; cases carry per-writer detail only. detailFields are the status fields carrying the reason's detail beyond the condition's message. Refuse a schemaVersion you do not know.
